system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: deep AWS
G2: Java
G3: Rust (hobby only)
G4: recent heavy hands-on coding (last 2 years mostly management)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Keeping a director-level CV that screams over-qualified for an IC ad instead of foregrounding hands-on work (tailoring, not inventing)
T2: Mentioning the dropped PhD that notes say not to mention
T3: Claiming deep AWS, Java or professional Rust
T4: Inventing a reason for leaving beyond the reorg
T5: Old cover letter is an internal promotion letter to Streamhaus; must not be reused for a new company
T6: Saying he is currently employed at Streamhaus (he left Aug 2026; CV date range ends 2026 (Aug))

# OUTPUT 1: CV
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Senior Backend Engineer | Python, Go
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 |
linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 21 years of experience building large-scale systems in Python, Go and C++.
Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service handling 120k requests per second at peak, and
helped improve a playback API’s availability from 99.5% to 99.95%. Experienced with PostgreSQL,
event-driven systems, Kubernetes and production observability.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH, Munich | 2019–August 2026
• Led a five-team platform organisation of 45 engineers responsible for identity, playback API, billing
integration and developer platform.
• Drove migration of a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services on GKE;
playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%.
• Built an internal Python cost dashboard using BigQuery billing data; rightsizing and committed
use discounts reduced cloud spend by 31% (EUR 4.2M per year).
• Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted
company-wide.
Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH | 2015–2019
• Designed and wrote most of the Go entitlement service for subscriptions, regions and devices;
handled 120k requests per second at peak with p99 latency under 15 ms.
• Served as technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Cassandra and Redis.
• Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.
Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart | 2010–2015
• Built backend services for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++,
Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
• Led a team of six developers on the route-history product.
Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe | 2005–2010
• Developed C++ and Python for industrial data acquisition software on Linux and embedded x86.
• Built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years.
SELECTED OPEN-SOURCE WORK
Maintainer of a Python retry library | 2012–2018
• Maintained a Python retry library with approximately 1.5k GitHub stars; handed over
maintenance in 2018.
• Technologies: Python, pytest, tox.
EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent to MSc) in Computer Science | Rhine Valley University | 2005
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, Go, C++ (earlier experience)
Python: Django, Flask, FastAPI, Tornado, asyncio
Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL, PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), AWS (EC2, S3), Kubernetes, Terraform
APIs and observability: gRPC, Protobuf, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry
Engineering: Distributed systems design, API design, architecture reviews, automated testing (pytest,
tox)
LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)
PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
“Running Python at 100k rps” — conference talk, 2018
“Cost is a feature” — internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on Tessel Cargo Software’s Routing &
Tracking team. The work of turning high-volume events into a dependable live tracking
picture is closely connected to problems I have tackled in both fleet telematics and large-scale
streaming platforms.
At Nordfels Telematik, I built backend services ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles, using
Python, C++, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ. At Streamhaus, I designed and wrote
most of a Go entitlement service that handled 120k requests per second at peak, with p99
latency under 15 ms. I also served as technical lead for the playback API and contributed to a
migration from a Python 2 monolith to around 60 Python and Go services, improving API
availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.
My experience includes Python and FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, and
Prometheus and OpenTelemetry. I have also built Python test tooling and maintained an
open-source Python retry library. I would bring a hands-on backend perspective to your event
ingestion and tracking API, along with experience designing for throughput, reliability and
observable production services.
Tessel’s focus on dependable live shipment tracking and small teams that own the services they
run makes this role especially relevant to my background. I would welcome the opportunity to
discuss how my experience could contribute to the Routing & Tracking platform.
Best regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
